Interestingly, the concentration of 15S-HETE, a precursor of the lipoxins, which are reported to have anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving properties, was significantly (P < 0.05) increased in the skin areas treated with OXA and NaCl (237.4 ± 70.1 pg/mg), compared with the areas treated with OXA and 15-epi-LXA4 (89.3 ± 29.8 pg/mg) and the untreated control areas (75.8 ± 29.8 pg/mg) 24 hours after challenge. There was no significant difference between these values and the 15-HETE concentrations measured 6 hours after challenge (129.2 ± 69.9 pg/mg for skin areas treated with OXA and NaCl and 160.8 ± 76.2 pg/mg for skin areas treated with OXA and 15-epi-LXA4). However, pro-resolving lipid mediators (lipoxins, resolvins, maresins or protectins) could not be detected in inflamed skin.
